## AI

### Agent composer (`agent-composer`, ~78.8k tokens)

Agent composer that doubles as a control panel. A workspace beside it (`items`, `doc`) adds context (click an item, or select text and "Add to chat"; on phones it folds into a toggle and the bar shows icons only, its panels spanning the composer). Attach with +, drag and drop or paste (file chips with upload progress). Pick a permission mode, toggle connectors, choose the model with per-model speed/effort steps, and open advanced settings.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/agent-composer.tsx
- Exports: AgentComposer
- Embeds: ApprovalCard, AttachmentChip, Badge, Button, Citation, Collapse, CopyButton, FloatingPanel, FormFieldContext, Icon, IconButton, InlineCode, Kbd, MagnetBubble, MagnetMarks, Markdown, MenuItem, MessageActions, MessageParts, PromptInput, Reasoning, ScrollEdges, SendButton, ShimmerText, Slider, Slot, SourceList, Spinner, StreamingText, Switch, ToolCard, TypingDots
- npm: motion, react

### Agent plan (`agent-plan`, ~9.9k tokens)

Plan first, then live progress. Pass `steps` with statuses to drive it yourself, or plain labels and it runs itself: Run shows "Step i of n", stays disabled while running, then offers "Run again".

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/agent-plan.tsx
- Exports: AgentPlan
- Embeds: Button, Icon, Progress, Slot, Spinner, StatusIcon
- npm: motion, react

### Agent transit map (`agent-transit-map`, ~52.4k tokens)

Live multi-agent "transit map", driven by the same WorkflowEngine as StateMachine. The Indexing loop and the Intake endpoint fire events into a queue (drawn on the map, under Intake); jobs start as slots free up and travel their state graph along the drawn lines, bends included. Agents take one job at a time: the others line up on the incoming line with a counter, and track segments warm up (grey, amber, red) as tokens pile onto them. Orchestrators route with guards, Product forks reviews and joins them, endpoints emit follow-up triggers. Human and Risk stations wait for approval when human-in-the-loop is on: the station gets a countdown ring and an approval card floats beside it, over the map, so nothing on the page moves. Pause, speed and max-jobs controls, fire-event chips, and a live trace table (time, tokens, USD) whose connectors link a follow-up job to the job that triggered it: hover a row, or press its job button, to follow that job on the map. The still drawing renders once; tokens and the train are composited layers moved every frame without re-rendering (30 fps on touch screens); the panels refresh about 8 times a second, and only the parts that changed. Reduced motion places tokens at their stations without travel. On phones the map keeps a readable size and scrolls sideways inside the card, as does the trace table. Pass `machines` whose stations are the map's (the sample is `AGENT_WORKFLOWS` / `AGENT_WORKFLOW_ORDER` in `@lyndon/ui/examples`); without any, the map is drawn with no traffic.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/agent-transit-map.tsx
- Exports: AgentTransitMap
- Embeds: Badge, Button, Chip, FormFieldContext, Icon, IconButton, MagnetBubble, MagnetMarks, ScrollEdges, Slider, Slot, Spinner, Switch, WorkflowEngine
- npm: motion, react, react-dom

### AI canvas (`ai-canvas`, ~27.8k tokens)

Chat on the left, a living document on the right. Asking for a change streams the edit into the file: added lines type in highlighted, removed lines strike through and collapse. Toggle Code/Preview (the preview is a sandboxed iframe), step through versions, copy, click or tap a line (or arrow to it and press Enter) to "Ask about line N", or use the suggestion chips. Below 768px chat and document stack, rows grow to finger height on touch, and the document scrolls into view while an edit streams in. A pill shows line count and version. The preview loads nothing remote (CSP in the frame); `allowRemote` lets https images in. Starts empty: pass `initial`, and either `respond` (your model: return the new document and a reply) or scripted `edits` (matched by prompt, else offered in order). The showcase content is `AI_CANVAS_SAMPLE` in `@lyndon/ui/examples`.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/ai-canvas.tsx
- Exports: AICanvas
- Embeds: ActiveIndicator, Badge, Button, Chip, CopyButton, FormFieldContext, Icon, IconButton, ScrollEdges, SegmentedControl, SendButton, Slot, Spinner, TypingDots
- npm: motion, react

### Ai renderers provider (`ai-renderers-provider`, ~773 tokens)

Supplies AiRenderers to every MessageParts below it (props given to a component win).

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/ai-renderers-provider.tsx
- Exports: AiRenderersProvider
- npm: react

### AI streams (useAiChat) (`ai-stream`, ~8.9k tokens)

The AI message model with parts (text, reasoning, tools, sources, files, data) and useAiChat, which streams from a ReadableStream, an AsyncIterable or an AI SDK UI message stream, with stop via AbortSignal.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/ai-stream.tsx

- npm: react

### Approval card (`approval-card`, ~9.8k tokens)

An approval prompt for an action the host wants to run: the tool, a summary, recipients and arguments exactly as given (shown as data, never as markup), with Deny and Approve. Approve is disabled for the first 500 ms so a click aimed at something else can't land on it as the card appears. It only reports the decision: run the action in `onDecide` (or in useAiChat's `onApprovalRequest`), never before.

### Conversation (`conversation`, ~15.3k tokens)

The scrolling message log. Stays pinned to the newest message while replies stream, unless the person scrolled up; then a "Jump to latest" button floats at the bottom (it never moves the layout). Give it a height (className, e.g. `h-[420px]`) so streaming never pushes the page. `busy` sets aria-busy; the log itself is not a live region, so screen readers aren't read every token (announce a summary yourself). Past `virtualizeAfter` children (default 60; give each a stable `key`, e.g. the message id) it renders only the messages in view, measuring their real heights, still pinned to the bottom while the last one grows and keeping your place when older ones are prepended.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/conversation.tsx
- Exports: Conversation, useStickToBottom, aiNearBottom
- Embeds: Icon
- npm: motion, react, react-dom

### Message (`message`, ~36.9k tokens)

One message. A user message is a bubble on the inline end (the right in LTR, the left in RTL; its text as plain text, attachments as tiles above); an assistant message sits on the start side with a name row (`avatar`, `name`) and its MessageParts, then `actions` once it stopped streaming; a system message is a quiet centred line. Pass the same handlers (and `renderers`) as MessageParts.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/message.tsx
- Exports: Message

- npm: motion, react

### Message actions (`message-actions`, ~11.0k tokens)

The row under an answer: "Stopped" when it was cut short, Copy (`text`, read when clicked), thumbs up / down (controlled `rating` + `onRate`, or uncontrolled), Regenerate or Retry (`onRetry`), and anything you add (`children`, e.g. a version switcher).

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/message-actions.tsx
- Exports: MessageActions
- Embeds: Button, CopyButton, Icon, IconButton, Slot, Spinner
- npm: motion, react

### Message parts (`message-parts`, ~36.2k tokens)

Renders a message's parts in order: text as Markdown (or through `renderers.text`; links through safeUrl, `[n]` is a Citation of the message's n-th source), reasoning as Reasoning, tool calls as ToolCard (approvals go to `onDecideTool`; data through `renderers.value`), files as attachment tiles, errors with a Retry (`onRetry`), and `data` parts through `renderData` (nothing by default). Sources are collected into numbered chips at the end. Model text never reaches the DOM as HTML. `renderers` (or an AiRenderersProvider above) adds code highlighting and JsonViewer: `<MessageParts message={m} renderers={AI_RICH_RENDERERS} />`.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/message-parts.tsx
- Exports: MessageParts
- Embeds: ApprovalCard, AttachmentChip, Badge, Button, Citation, Collapse, CopyButton, Icon, InlineCode, Markdown, Reasoning, ScrollEdges, ShimmerText, Slot, SourceList, Spinner, ToolCard, TypingDots
- npm: motion, react

### Model comparison (`model-comparison`, ~14.4k tokens)

Same prompt, several models streamed side by side at their own speeds: thinking dots, first-token time, tokens/s and cost. Vote for the best answer (a toast confirms). Run restarts all of them. `autoRun` starts the first run by itself the first time the comparison scrolls into view.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/model-comparison.tsx
- Exports: ModelComparison
- Embeds: Button, Icon, IconButton, Slot, Spinner, TypingDots
- npm: motion, react

### Permission request (`permission-request`, ~20.3k tokens)

Ask before acting: say what, to whom, and why. Preview the payload (`recipients`, `total`, `list` and the `draft`), edit the draft, then Allow or Deny. The host does the work: `onDecide(allowed, always, draft)` gets the draft as edited, and may return a promise that settles when sending finished (false or a rejection shows "Not sent"). Pass `progress` ({ sent, total }) to show "n of 12 delivered" while it runs. With `onUndo`, a countdown ring offers Undo for `undoSeconds`; "Nothing reached the recipients" is shown only when onUndo resolves true. Every state swap animates height.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/permission-request.tsx
- Exports: PermissionRequest
- Embeds: AnimatedNumber, AutoHeight, Avatar, Badge, Button, CheckMark, Checkbox, CheckboxBox, Collapse, FormFieldContext, Icon, Progress, Slot, Spinner
- npm: motion, react

### Prompt input (`prompt-input`, ~15.2k tokens)

The prompt box for chats. Grows with its text up to `maxHeight`, then scrolls. Enter sends (never mid IME composition), Shift+Enter adds a line. Attach with +, paste or drag and drop; images preview through object URLs that are revoked when removed or sent. Optional model picker (`models`, `model`, `onModelChange`) and your own buttons (`tools`). While `status` is submitted or streaming, Send turns into Stop (`onStop`). `onSubmit(text, files)` may return false to keep the draft. Text is controlled (`value`/`onChange`, e.g. useAiChat's input) or not.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/prompt-input.tsx

- Embeds: Button, Icon, IconButton, Slot, Spinner
- npm: motion, react

### Thinking steps (`thinking-steps`, ~10.8k tokens)

Reasoning as a vertical stepper. Static (pass `status` per step) or `autoPlay`: starts when scrolled into view, types the current step's detail and pops in its source chips while finished steps fold to one line (with their time; click one to read it again), and fills the connector. The list reserves the height of its tallest step up front, so playing never pushes the page. The header counts "Thinking… 3.2s", then reads "Thought for Xs · N steps"; click it to fold the steps away. `autoCollapse` folds them by itself when done (it changes the height, so use it where nothing sits below, e.g. the end of a chat). Change `replayKey` to run it again. Paused while off screen.

## Other

### Chart with journal (`chart-with-journal`, ~23.1k tokens)

A chart and its journal side by side (pattern H), linked both ways: hovering, focusing or tapping a tag on either side lights it on the other, and the list scrolls the lit row into view without moving focus. Below 640 px of width the list stacks under the chart. The chart is a render prop, so any annotated chart works: `<ChartWithJournal tags={tags} chart={link => <Chart data={day} x="t" series={…} annotations={{ ...link, style: 'dots' }} />} />`.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/chart-with-journal.tsx

- Embeds: Button, Icon, IconButton, Slot, Spinner, TagGlyph, TagJournal, VirtualList
- npm: motion, react, react-dom

### Git graph (`git-graph`, ~90.2k tokens)

Commit history graph (like VS Code's Git Graph or GitKraken): a LaneGraph preset with refs, author, relative date and hash columns, virtualised for 100k commits. Click or Enter opens details (a side panel, a sheet on phones: message, parents, refs, files and diffs from `loadCommit`); Shift+click a second commit compares the range (`loadDiff`). Hover or focus lights the first-parent ancestry. Keys: ↑/↓ rows, ← parent, → child, Home/End, PageUp/Down, `/` search, n/N next/previous match, Enter open, Escape close; Shift+F10, right-click or long-press opens the actions menu. Search, branch filter, first-parent and hide-merged views in the toolbar. New commits on top keep the reader's place.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/git-graph.tsx
- Exports: GitGraph
- Embeds: ActiveIndicator, Avatar, Badge, Button, Chip, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuRoot, ContextMenuTrigger, CopyButton, DialogClose, DialogRoot, DialogTitle, Diff, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuRoot, DropdownMenuTrigger, FloatingPanel, FormFieldContext, Icon, IconButton, InlineCode, Kbd, LaneGraph, LaneGutter, Markdown, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuItem, MenuLabel, MenuSeparator, ModalLayer, OverlayPortal, PopoverContent, PopoverRoot, PopoverTrigger, ScrollEdges, SegmentedControl, SheetContent, SheetHeader, Slot, Spinner
- npm: motion, react, react-dom

### Lane graph (`lanes`, ~25.4k tokens)

Any DAG as rows: layoutLanes (headless: order, lanes, colours and each row's edges, O(n · lanes)), LaneGutter (one row's SVG slice, stretches to tall rows) and LaneGraph (a virtualised list of gutter + your renderRow, with selection, hover ancestry, keyboard moves along edges and live inserts). GitGraph is a preset of it.

### Magnet marks (`magnet-marks`, ~1.7k tokens)

The track decorations: a tick for each point (and each zone centre), a tinted band for each zone. Put it inside the track (it fills it, absolutely positioned, aria-hidden). `inset` is the thumb's radius in px when the thumb's centre stops short of the track's ends (native range inputs), so ticks line up with it. Positions are logical (inset-inline-start), so they mirror with the track in RTL and stay put inside an LTR island.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/magnet-marks.tsx
- Exports: MagnetMarks

### State ribbon (`state-ribbon`, ~16.5k tokens)

What you were doing all day in one strip (pattern F: sleep stages, Toggl and RescueTime day bars): contiguous states coloured by kind, optional pins above for point tags (merged into counts when crowded) and bars below for spans. Slivers too thin to see get a minimum width, runs of them merge into one "mixed" segment, and on touch every thin mark has a finger-sized hit area. Hover, focus or tap for state and duration. Keyboard: one Tab stop, ←/→ along a row, ↑/↓ between pins, states and bars. `size="compact"` suits phones and widgets.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/state-ribbon.tsx
- Exports: StateRibbon
- Embeds: TagGlyph, TagTooltip
- npm: motion, react

### Swimlanes (`swimlanes`, ~14.9k tokens)

One lane per kind of tag on a shared time axis (pattern E: Dynatrace annotation tracks, LifeLines): dots for point tags, rounded pills for spans, an icon and label at the start of each lane, an optional chart on top (`top`) aligned to the same `start`–`end`. Dots closer than `mergePx` merge into a count chip; empty lanes say "None" (or hide with `hideEmpty`); more than `maxLanes` lanes scroll. Hover, focus or tap a mark for its tooltip. Keyboard: the lanes are one Tab stop, ←/→ move along a lane, ↑/↓ between lanes, Enter selects, Escape clears. Link it to other views with `activeId` / `onActiveChange`. The plot runs left to right in every locale; labels and tooltips follow the locale.

- File: https://lantos1618.github.io/oneshot-ui/files/swimlanes.tsx
- Exports: Swimlanes
- Embeds: TagGlyph, TagTooltip
- npm: motion, react

### Tag glyph (`tag-glyph`, ~1.1k tokens)

A tag's icon in a coloured ring; `active` grows it with a halo, `more` adds a "+N" badge on its end side (timeTagBadge wide). Decorative unless given a role.

### Tag journal (`tag-journal`, ~22.5k tokens)

A time-ordered list of tags (pattern H: Oura and WHOOP journals): time, glyph, label and detail, optionally grouped by hour, virtualised so long days stay fast. Hovering or focusing a row lights that tag (`activeId` / `onActiveChange`), and when the active tag changes elsewhere (a linked chart) the list scrolls it into view without moving focus. `onEdit` / `onDelete` add labelled icon buttons. Keyboard: the list is one Tab stop (then the row's buttons), ↑/↓ move between rows, Home/End jump, Enter selects, Escape clears.
